content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves the Isaiah 7:14 link by comparing CR2's chain with DR3's pressed sign, so the chain-collision rule K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the sign itself does not state the mechanism.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"never verse by verse: one reading forbids deciding a chain collision by whether a single verse states the point; the other allows noting a single verse's silence as part of footing. I applied the first reading.","why":"The judge marks the link underdetermined because the sign verse itself does not state the mechanism, which is a verse-by-verse/stating-verse test rather than a weighing of the two chains by footing."}
